children: Australian stocks look set to edge higher at the open despite a soft lead from the U.S., where higher oil prices and doubts over artificial-intelligence profitability weighed on major indices. ASX futures are up by 0.2% ahead of Friday's open, suggesting that the S&P/ASX 200 could recover some ground lost in the prior session. The benchmark index fell 0.8% Thursday, dropping into the red for the week. Ahead of the open, gold miner Alkane Resourses reiterated its annual production and cost guidance. In the U.S., the DJIA added 0.1%, but the S&P 500 lost 0.5% and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 1.25%. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)
